Change c0104. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. V.

Context before (unchanged): I traversed the streets, without any clear conception of where I was, or what I was doing.

1818 text: My heart palpitated in the sickness of fear; and I hurried on with irregular steps, not daring to look about me: Like one who, on a lonely road, Doth walk in fear and dread, And, having once turn'd round, walks on, And turns no more his head; Because he knows a frightful fiend Doth close behind him tread.

1831 text: My heart palpitated in the sickness of fear; and I hurried on with irregular steps, not daring to look about me:— "Like one who, on a lonely road, Doth walk in fear and dread, And, having once turned round, walks on, And turns no more his head; Because he knows a frightful fiend Doth close behind him tread."

Diff: My heart palpitated in the sickness of fear; and I hurried on with irregular steps, not daring to look about me: {+—"+} Like one who, on a lonely road, Doth walk in fear and dread, And, having once [-turn'd-] {+turned+} round, walks on, And turns no more his head; Because he knows a frightful fiend Doth close behind him tread. {+"+}

Context after (unchanged): Continuing thus, I came at length opposite to the inn at which the various diligences and carriages usually stopped.

result.rationale: Only change in the verse is 'turn'd' to 'turned', a spelling modernization with no change in meaning. The added dash and quotation marks mark the Coleridge quotation typographically, which is a punctuation matter.
